title: Toki
build: Ocean type 1 cartridge, 16 banks of 8 KB (128 KB)

records.c: The first 11 bytes of Stage 2's data block, loaded from $0C01. Bytes 2-4 are the stage's three background colours ($D021-$D023; stage_setup_tables copies them to bg_colour0-2): 00, 09, 08 here. Byte 5 (07) is the number of the last section, which track_stage_section and init_round_state read. Bytes 6-7 ($87FA) point into cartridge bank 0 to the 64 bytes of stream records that load_stage_bank_records copies to $0100. Bytes 8-9 ($8902) point to the list of animation ids that the helper at $06E6 searches, and byte 10 (3D) is that list's last index. Bytes 0 and 1 (9B, 22) are read by nothing in play.

The 22 bytes $0C0C-$0C21 are Stage 2's eleven table pointers; stage_setup_tables copies them to $2A-$3F (map_row_lo_ptr, map_row_hi_ptr, block_chars_ptr, block_props_ptr, path_table_ptr, $34, script_ptr_a, script_ptr_b, anim_lo_ptr, anim_hi_ptr and $3E). Their values here are $1C68, $1C8A, $0D32, $1CAC, $1DD8, $1FA6, $20DB, $2108, $2080, $2042, $20BE.

Colour of each character code in Stage 2, 256 bytes, indexed by the character (screen code) found in the screen buffers. recolour_screen copies the entry for every one of the 840 playfield characters into colour RAM. Only the low nibble reaches colour RAM, and a value of 8 or more turns on multicolour for that character, since the playfield runs in multicolour text mode ($D016 bit 4).

Table of section record addresses for Stage 2: one word for each of its 8 sections, $0D22-$0D31, starting $1D0B, $1D24, $1D3D and on, each 25 bytes on. store_section_index indexes it with section_index times 2, track_stage_section with the next and the previous section's index times 2, and init_round_state with the last section's ($0C06); stage_setup_tables reads the first word through $24.

The map block table of Stage 2: four screen characters for each of 95 block numbers (upper left, upper right, lower left, lower right), $0D32-$0EAD, pointed to by block_chars_ptr ($2E). The table's length depends on the stage.

The block numbers of Stage 2's map, one byte for each block position, from $0EAE to $1C67. map_row_lo/hi_table give each of the 34 rows' start (first $0E9E, $0F39, $0FD4); rows differ in length, and a row's pointer is biased by the row's first column, so the byte for block column x is at the row pointer plus x. Each byte indexes block_chars and block_props_table.
Bytes $12AE-$16AD of map_rows_data ($12AE is 1024 bytes in).
Bytes $16AE-$1AAD of map_rows_data ($16AE is 2048 bytes in).
Bytes $1AAE-$1C67 of map_rows_data ($1AAE is 3072 bytes in).

Map row address table, low bytes: 34 entries $1C68-$1C89, one for each row of Stage 2's map. map_row_lo_ptr ($2A) points here and stage_setup_tables copies the pointer from $0C0C. The high bytes are the 34 bytes at $1C8A.

Map row address table, high bytes: 34 entries $1C8A-$1CAB. map_row_hi_ptr ($2C) points here and stage_setup_tables copies the pointer from $0C0E. The low bytes are map_row_lo_table at $1C68; a row starts at hi:lo.

Map block properties of Stage 2, one byte for each block number: 95 bytes $1CAC-$1D0A, matching the 95 four-character blocks of block_chars ($0D32-$0EAD). block_props_ptr ($30) points here. Bit 0 solid, bit 1 harmful, bits 2 and 3 slopes, bit 5 enter mode 1, as block_property_at and the terrain probes test them. The values present are $00, $01, $04, $05, $10, $11, $40, $41.

The 8 section records of Stage 2, 25 bytes each, $1D0B-$1DD2: section_table ($0D22) holds their addresses. Each record begins with the follow zone (zone_left, zone_right, zone_top, zone_bottom) and the view limits that update_view_scroll reads through section_ptr ($26), and holds the flags byte at offset $16 (section_scroll_flags); the rest of the 25 bytes is not decoded here.
Stage 2 block bytes $1DD3-$1DD7 between two tables; role not established (5 bytes).

Table of path data addresses that path_table_ptr ($32) points to, indexed by obj_arc_state; the pointer is one below the first entry in the stage 1 table, so the table's first word may start at $1DD9. The pointer at $34 is $1FA6. The area from $1DD8 to $1FA5 is 462 bytes; the format of its words is as in stage 1's path_address_table.

The table the pointer at $34 (a copy of $0C16, here $1FA6) points to: script command 22 ($B722) reads it through ($34) at $B72D to find the record of an object it sets up; its first word is $1FA8. In stage 1 the first path data and these records lie together in this area; where this stage's path data ends is not established. $1FC0-$2007 is not record data: it holds the tables of stage2_spawn_projectile_burst ($BD76), four pointers at $1FC0 ($1FC8, $1FD8, $1FE8, $1FF8; stage2_patch points $48/$49 at the first) to four 16-byte sets of x and y velocity words. The timed-step routine's tables follow at $2008.

Four 4-byte positions of Stage 2's timed-step routine at $BE73: an x word and a y word each ($0944/$0020, $08C4/$0010, $0874/$0020, $0924/$0018 here). When the step counter $2018 runs out, $BE73 advances $201A by 4 (wrapping at 16) and loads $E7/$E8 (x) and $E9/$EA (y) from the entry it points to.

Step counter of the timed-step routine at $BE73, counting 0 to 18 (19 steps). stage2_patch clears it at the start of a round; $BE73 stores the next step here, and at step 7 it sets $378A to 3 and the timer to 4 (the other steps only set the timer and value).

Frame timer of the timed-step routine at $BE73. stage2_patch loads it from $202E at the start of a round; $BE73 counts it down each time it runs with $378A negative, and on reaching zero moves to the next step and reloads it from stage2_sequence_timer_table.
Index (0, 4, 8 or 12) of the current entry of stage2_sequence_positions. stage2_patch clears it; $BE73 adds 4 each time the 19 steps finish, wrapping to 0 at 16.

19 bytes, one for each step of the timed-step routine at $BE73; the entry for the step is copied to $2E87 (stage2_patch loads the first, $42, at the start of a round). $2E87 is not code: in Stage 2 it lies in the last animation data block (the block at $2E78, after the stage's block). What the byte selects there is not established.
19 bytes, one for each step of the timed-step routine at $BE73: the number of frames the step lasts, copied to the timer $2019 when the step starts ($32, $04, $0C, $0C, $10, ... here).

Read index of stage2_spawn_projectile_burst ($BD76): it stores $FE here when it picks a new velocity set ($BDC1), then for each object it spawns adds 2 ($BDF0-$BDF5) and reads that object's x velocity word through ($48) at this index and its y velocity word 8 bytes further on. $00 in the snapshot. It follows stage2_sequence_timer_table, before anim_hi_table.

High bytes of the addresses of Stage 2's animation data blocks, 62 entries $2042-$207F indexed by animation number; anim_hi_ptr ($3C) points here. The low bytes are the 62 bytes of anim_lo_table at $2080.
Low bytes of the addresses of Stage 2's animation data blocks, 62 entries $2080-$20BD, indexed by animation number; anim_lo_ptr ($3A) points here. The partner of anim_hi_table.

The eleventh table of Stage 2, which $3E points to (stored by stage_setup_tables from $0C20): the hit reactions 0 and 1 ($A8FA, $A8D8) replace an object's obj_anim_num with the entry at that index, so it maps an animation number to the animation the object switches to when hit. It starts at $20BE.

Low bytes of the addresses of Stage 2's object movement scripts: 45 entries $20DB-$2107, the table that script_ptr_a ($36) points to. object_script_step loads the pair (script_ptr_a, script_ptr_b) into $E3/$E4 and then reads the script byte at ($E3) + obj_script_pos ($379C,x). The high bytes are script_addr_hi.
High bytes of the addresses of Stage 2's object movement scripts: 45 entries $2108-$2134, the table that script_ptr_b ($38) points to; the low bytes are script_addr_lo.

Object movement script bytes of Stage 2, from $2135; the scripts start between $2135 and $23EF. A byte below $80 is a command number: object_script_step looks it up in script_cmd_lo/hi at $B33C/$B35F and runs it; a byte with bit 7 set is a move (low four bits the direction, next byte the repeat count).
Bytes $2535-$2683 of script_data ($2535 is 1024 bytes in).

Stage 2 entry for table indexes 6, 10, 20, 21 and 25. It runs only on frames where frame_count & 6 is zero and steps a counter held in obj_off_y,x. While the counter is negative it sets $2D3E, $2D4A and $2D46 (bytes of Stage 2's animation data, probably frame entries) and $377B (obj_off_y of object 51) and counts up; on reaching zero it sets the other values, calls the random number step $A8C9, uses its result & 6 to pick a 2-byte pointer from $1FC0 into $48/$49 and sets the counter to 4. While positive it counts down and, each step, spawns one temp object: velocities are read through ($48) at the index in $2041 into temp_vel_x/y_lo/hi, temp_life is $FF, and the new slot (E2 = counter + temp_first) gets obj_kind $20, obj_state $19, anim and move_bits fields, x = $E7/$E8 + 8, y = $E9/$EA + $15, and zeroed arc_state and obj_hit_* arrays. When the count runs out it stores $F0, which is not an end: the negative branch counts $F0 up to zero (16 steps) and then starts the next burst.
Positive-counter branch: decrement obj_off_y,x; if it went negative store $F0 and return, otherwise fall into the spawn code at $BDE4.

Stage 2 entry for table index 7. Reads $378A (slot $42's obj_off_y, probably a boss part timer). If negative, it counts $2019 down and advances through step tables at $2008, $201B and $202E (loading $E7-$EA from $2008,y and writing $2E87), ending the script at step 7 by setting $378A=3 and $3310=$FE. If non-negative it decrements the value into obj_off_y,x. When that goes below zero it counts $2019 down, spawning one object per count into slots indexed by $2019 (with a direction value $07, $0B or $0F chosen by comparing $3CD0/$3D2D/$3C16/$3C73 with player_box_left/right), and when it runs out sets obj_arc_state,x=9, obj_off_y,x=$FF and obj_motion,x=$12. Ends with $14 (obj_first) = $3E on the spawn path.
Non-negative $378A path: subtract 1 and store into obj_off_y,x, or fall to the spawn/finish logic when it goes below zero.

Spawn one object into object 62 + $2019: sets $378A=3, chooses a direction ($0F, $0B or $07, stored in obj_dir of that object) by comparing object 66's hit box ($3C16/$3C73 left, $3CD0/$3D2D right) with player_box_left/right, then initialises many per-object arrays at index y (including zeroed hit-box arrays) and places it at $E7-$EA plus $18 in x. Ends by setting obj_first ($14) to $3E.

The character set of the playfield for Stage 2, $C000-$C777 (1912 bytes loaded by the stage's character set directory entry): eight pixel rows for each character, starting at character $00 (VIC bank 3, $D018 $21 or $31). stage_load copies it from the cartridge at stage start.
Bytes $C400-$C777 of stage_charset ($C400 is 1024 bytes in).
